answer.evidence: The skulls are arranged in depth with the upper skull's dome/cranium visible for 3 pixel rows (rows 0-2) above the eye sockets, providing appropriate 3/4 downward-angled perspective for rounded organic shapes without flat front elevation or isometric side faces.

All three skulls are drawn in pure front elevation with eyes and jaws facing straight at the camera. The top of the cranium above the eye sockets is only 2 pixels tall (e.g. rows 1-2 on the top skull, rows 6-7 on the lower skulls), lacking the foreshortened top dome expected from a 45-degree top-down perspective.
